full_judgment:
We have taken a similar view in Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 96 of 1978. Wherein it has been held that non-compliance with the mandatory requirement of the Emergency Powers Rule, 1975 while making a detention order under rule 5(1) (a) invalidates the detention. 

 6. So, on this ground alone the detention of the detention is liable to be declared illegal and improper. The first order of detention under rule 5(I) (a) being found Illegal, subsequent order extending the said detention are also void and illegal. As regards the second contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner we have perused the grounds of detention as stated in Annexure 'Z' to the supplementary affidavit and the fact stated in the affidavit in-opposition. It appears that the detenu, in a reception accorded to him on 23.12.77 in the Tejgaon Awami League Office, at the instance of the local Sramik League, after his release from detention, delivered speeches narrating problems of the worker and raised some demands. The learned Deputy Attorney General produced an office file and we have perused the same, but there it nothing in the said file to show the exact wordings of the speeches said to have, been delivered by the detenu. There is no other instance of any specific act which can be termed as prejudicial, calling for an order of detention under rule 5(1) (a) of the Emergency Powers Rules, 1975. For the aforesaid reason. We are of opinion that the grounds furnished cannot be a reasonable basis for the satisfaction of the detaining authority in pasting an order under rule 5(1)(a), We, therefore, hold that the detenu Mahmudur Rahman alias Rahim is illegally and improperly detained. Accordingly, we direct that the detenu Mahmudur Rahman alias Belayet be set at liberty forthwith, if not wanted in connection with any other case.
